summary: Oregon is strict on exotic wildlife generally, but it explicitly carves the roof rat out: OAR 635-056-0020 names 'Rat — Rattus norvegicus and R. rattus' as a DOMESTIC animal exempt from the entire nonnative-wildlife scheme, and ORS 609.305's 'exotic animal' permit definition excludes rodents. So no ODFW or exotic-animal permit is needed to keep, breed, or transfer a captive-bred roof rat. The only requirement is a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection when importing one (a 'pocket pet') from out of state. Never release one.

keep.why: OAR 635-056-0020 ('Animals Exempt from These Rules') names 'Rat — Rattus norvegicus and R. rattus' as a domestic animal, removing R. rattus from ODFW's prohibited/controlled/noncontrolled nonnative-wildlife scheme entirely; ORS 609.305 also excludes rodents from the exotic-animal permit. No permit to keep one.

breed.why: As a domestic-exempt animal, breeding needs no ODFW permit, and rodents are outside the ORS 609 exotic-animal scheme. Commercial pet-shop operations meet ODA sanitation/recordkeeping standards (OAR 603-015) but face no species prohibition.

sell_give.why: A domestic-exempt animal isn't subject to ODFW sale restrictions; ORS 609.305 excludes rodents. Commercial pet shops keep sale records (OAR 603-015-0060); free rehoming and small sales need no permit.

transport.why: Intrastate transport is unregulated (domestic-exempt). Importing a roof rat from out of state requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection within 30 days (ODA 'pocket pets' import rule). Never release a roof rat (ORS 498.052 bars releasing domestically raised/imported animals).
transport.governing_law: OAR 635-056-0020 (intrastate exempt); ODA pocket-pet import (OAR 603-011); ORS 498.052 (no-release).

restrictions.summary: Importing a pet rat into Oregon requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (within 30 days; 'pocket pet' rule). No CVI for in-state movement. Never release one.
restrictions.where_to_file: Oregon Dept of Agriculture, Animal Health
